10                Yes, today I stand to recognize the 

11   legacy and the contributions of Cesar Chavez.  

12   Many of us may very often hear the phrase, the 

13   motto "Yes, we can," "Sí, se puede," not knowing 

14   that it was first started out on the West Coast 

15   by this mountain of a man who moved to organize 

16   farmworkers, grape pickers, out in the California 

17   region.

18                He was known for his keen leadership 

19   style and his constant struggle to protect the 

20   rights of farmworkers in California and 

21   throughout the United States.

22                Like Gandhi and Martin Luther King, 

23   Cesar Chavez believed in and carried out his 

24   struggle adhering to the principles of 

25   nonviolence.  His many acts of protest and
